description: Last-resort fallback for a real user mistake (cp_loss >= 50) with a clear better_move but NO shape / NO principle / NO firing R-rule. Severity tier respects [[cp-loss-is-not-material]] — never translate cp_loss to 'X pawns lost'. Variants are layered (Mohit 2026-05-21): (1) detector-driven variants when curriculum/blocked_pawn/board_state produced a fact — highest priority; (2) position-eval variants when user is decisively winning or losing — reframe instead of criticize; (3) bare engine-speak default at cp_loss >= 100; (4) silent for low-cp_loss positional preferences in balanced positions.

fact_glossary.severity_phrase: Authored phrase picked from severity_phrases via severity_tiers
fact_glossary.user_is_winning: true when user_eval_after >= +200cp from user POV (decisive winning territory). Triggers the with_winning_position variant for non-tactical mistakes — reframe as encouragement instead of criticism.
fact_glossary.user_is_losing: true when user_eval_after <= -200cp from user POV. Triggers with_losing_position — reframe as context (you were already losing) instead of blame.
fact_glossary.curriculum_deviation_clause: Hand-authored wrong_feedback from opening_curriculum.json — surfaced by V5 when the user deviated from a curated opening tree. Highest variant priority.
fact_glossary.curriculum_expected_move: Book-theory move the tree expected (used as backup display).
fact_glossary.curriculum_opening_name: Matched opening's name (used as backup display).
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_file: File letter of a user pawn whose advance was blocked by the played piece move. Set by principle_blocked_pawn detector — names an opening principle violation.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_square: Target square the blocked pawn would have advanced to.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_would_support: Central pawn square the blocked pawn would have supported diagonally.
fact_glossary.board_state_clause: Pre-rendered string from board_state_describer (1-3 facts joined).

variants.with_blocked_pawn_supports: {move_san} {severity_phrase} — it blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn. {best_move} would have supported your {blocked_pawn_would_support} pawn.
variants.with_blocked_pawn: {move_san} {severity_phrase} — it blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn from advancing to {blocked_pawn_square}. {best_move} was better.
variants.with_winning_position: {move_san} is fine — you're still winning. {best_move} would have kept the pressure on.
variants.with_losing_position: {move_san} doesn't change much — you were already losing. {best_move} would have made the loss slower.
